_review.how: Blind to condition and outcome, from contamination_review.py's output and a scripted listing of every flagged call's full command (harness/contamination_detail.py), checked for content-reading verbs on outside paths: every cat, head, tail, sort, grep, sed, python or similar in a flagged call is a pipe stage on a listing, and no flagged call executed another trial's tool or read a saved tool-output file. 69 of the 70 flagged calls are Bash find/ls listings; one is a WebSearch.
_review.git_or_bd_flags: transcripts.py's git_or_bd flag marks 6 trials (384f8e, 84b979, 86bf3a, 8cf37c, 99abfc, d63416). All are false positives: the commands contain 'git' only in echo text ('no git used') or a 'test -d .git' check. No trial ran git or bd, so none read the notebook repository.
_review.rule: Pre-registered: reading a file's contents outside the trial (other than system or library files) or any network request excludes; listings don't. 66 flagged trials are kept and 79afad (web search) is excluded. The sensitivity analysis drops all 67 flagged trials.
_review.infrastructure: Pre-registered: a trial that hit an infrastructure failure is excluded. 005 had none, so analyze.py had no rule for it. Read, before unblinding, as a failure during the task, before the result was handed back: 025db7 and d5fc47 each had one interrupted API response mid-task and are excluded; 5d9053's came after its hand-back and it is kept. The alternative reading, keeping all three, is reported as an unplanned sensitivity check.
